solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I shall start getting stuck in with nothing on menu

indicators.note: getting stuck in tells us the first pieces are lodged inside the word for naked

parts.note: with nothing on means bare, unclothed
I shall contracts to I'll
the start of a race is the off

explanation.surface: Someone announces they will tuck into dinner while naked, menu in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting stuck in' looks like tucking into a meal, but it is the container signal. 'Start' as a noun is 'the off', the moment a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill of fare is an old-fashioned name for the list of dishes a restaurant offers.

clue.text: Non-believer putting diamonds down for playing area

indicators.note: putting means placing the card-suit letter somewhere new within the word
in a down entry, down means lower in the column, so the letter goes to the very end

parts.note: an infidel is someone who rejects a faith
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: An atheist lays down diamonds in a card game to win a playing area.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light, 'down' means lower in the column, so the D of INFIDEL slides to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket and baseball the infield is the part of the pitch nearest the batter, a region of play.

clue.text: Awfully bright learner gets university to deliver

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate abbreviation
to deliver, as in deliver us from evil, is to rid

explanation.surface: A student goes off to college to make a delivery, in garish colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid colours are glaringly, unpleasantly vivid, which is what awfully bright describes.

clue.text: Military cover wears out

definitions.meaning: combat dress worn by soldiers, their working uniform
tires or exhausts someone, a verb

explanation.surface: Army clothing that gets worn through.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun sense is soldiers' work clothing; the verb sense is to exhaust or tire someone.

clue.text: Splashdown that's insignificant

definitions.meaning: read playfully as a single drip falling into the sea
a tiny amount that makes no difference to the whole

explanation.surface: A space capsule's landing at sea proves unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: a splash down into the sea is literally one drop landing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an amount too small to matter compared with what is needed.

clue.text: Go green, turning yellow at first

indicators.note: turning signals that the letters of green are rearranged
at first takes only the opening letter of yellow

explanation.surface: Advice to become environmentally friendly, though the leaves turn yellow first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges GREEN into ENERG, then 'at first' adds Y from yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Go as a noun means vigour or drive, as in full of go, which is energy.

clue.text: Players squint

definitions.meaning: the actors in a play taken together
a squint or slight turn of the eye, an old sense

explanation.surface: Actors narrowing their eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The company of actors in a production is its cast, and a cast in the eye is a squint.

clue.text: Weapons carried around Tarsus initially worried St Paul

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means around or approximately

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of Tarsus
worried signals the letters of St Paul are churned up

explanation.surface: Weapons brought round Tarsus, the apostle's birthplace, troubled St Paul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried' is only a link. 'worried' turns ST PAUL into APULTS. Tarsus was St Paul's home town, which binds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Catapults are devices for hurling stones or missiles, a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Prevent doctor injecting a temporary substitute

parts.note: to prevent something is to stop it

indicators.note: injecting means the doctor's letters take the next piece inside them

parts.note: GP, a general practitioner, is a family doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor giving an injection to prevent illness as a temporary measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injecting' puts A inside GP to make GAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is something used for the time being until a proper replacement arrives.

clue.text: Hunter's trip ignoring outsiders some way off

indicators.note: ignoring outsiders means dropping the first and last letters of the trip

parts.note: a safari is an expedition to hunt or watch big game

explanation.surface: A big-game hunter sets off on an expedition far away, shunning strangers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring outsiders' strips S and I from SAFARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at a distance, far away from here.

clue.text: Wrong turning after country dance

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the country

parts.note: Turkey is a country

indicators.note: turning means the word for a legal wrong is read backwards

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A wrong turn taken after crossing the border into a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses TORT, a legal wrong, to give TROT.
explanation.definitionFit: The turkey trot is a ragtime-era American ballroom dance.

clue.text: Salt dosage in a stew

indicators.note: in a stew means agitated, signalling that the letters of dosage are jumbled

explanation.surface: A measured amount of salt goes into the stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like the seasoning, but it is the old-sailor sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a seasoned sailor, as is a sea dog.

clue.text: Twice each year leave capital

indicators.note: twice says the piece built from the next words appears two times

parts.note: PA, per annum, means each year
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Twice a year someone sets off from the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pago Pago is the capital city of American Samoa in the Pacific.

clue.text: Characteristic of a wandering hero? Yes, a Don's meandering

indicators.note: meandering signals the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: the possessive is read as a plain s on the end of Don

explanation.surface: A university don rambles on, agreeing he is like a roaming epic hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meandering' rearranges YES A DONS. The wandering hero is Odysseus, whose ten-year journey home is the Odyssey.
explanation.definitionFit: Odyssean describes anything like Odysseus or his long, roving voyage.

clue.text: Knees a bit wobbly? That could be fatal!

indicators.note: wobbly signals the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone feels weak at the knees, then realises the danger may be deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbly' rearranges KNEES A BIT; weak knees are also a symptom of venom.
explanation.definitionFit: A bite from a venomous snake can kill, so it is an example of something potentially fatal.

clue.text: Heading off where skiers may be bound

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the ski word is removed

parts.note: skiers are found on a slope

explanation.surface: Setting off to where skiers might be heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'headed for', but it is the definition, a long leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long, bounding strides.

clue.text: In good time I treat dicky bird

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters between the two abbreviations
dicky, British slang for weak or faulty, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone promptly treats a poorly bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dicky' is British slang for unsound, so it rearranges I TREAT to REATTI, which goes between G and T.
explanation.definitionFit: The great tit is a common European songbird of the tit family.

clue.text: Almost perfect impression

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: perfect means ideal

explanation.surface: A nearly flawless impression.
explanation.definitionFit: An impression is a notion or vague belief, which is an idea.

clue.text: Very active detectives holding a crowd up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the whole assembly is read bottom to top
holding means the detectives' letters wrap round the crowd

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police
a crowd is many people

explanation.surface: Energetic police detectives hold up a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the container signal and 'up' reverses the whole build, as this is a down light. CID is the British police's plain-clothes detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic describes someone or something full of energy and drive.

clue.text: Far from tender with vessel in distress

parts.note: the opposite of tender is hard
a ship is a sea vessel

explanation.surface: A tough boat in trouble at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship is suffering or privation, the state of being in distress.

clue.text: Some slim men seem huge

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some thin men appear enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means extremely large, a straightforward synonym of huge.

clue.text: Warner Bros' first canoe up the creek

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Bros'
up the creek, meaning in trouble, signals the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Hollywood studio Warner Bros sends its first canoe up a creek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warner' looks like the film studio but is the definition: something that warns. 'up the creek' rearranges CANOE to EACON.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal fire or light that warns of danger, so it is a warner.

clue.text: Californian backer backing one

parts.note: an angel is a financial backer of a show

indicators.note: backing means the word one is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A Californian investor supports one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses ONE to ENO.
explanation.definitionFit: An Angeleno is a resident of Los Angeles, so a Californian.

clue.text: Take on when birds go west

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as he left

indicators.note: go west means reading right to left in an across entry, so the birds are reversed

parts.note: emus are large flightless birds

explanation.surface: Something gets taken on when birds migrate westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go west' also hints at dying, but in an across light it reverses EMUS to SUME.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a role or responsibility is to take it on.

clue.text: River almost cut off

indicators.note: almost means the river's name loses its last letter

parts.note: the Severn is Britain's longest river

explanation.surface: A river nearly cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn is the longest river in Britain, flowing through Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever is to cut something off or apart.

clue.text: Confused since I'm not completely clued up

indicators.note: confused signals the letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving I and M

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled because they are not fully informed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' rearranges SINCE IM NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Omniscient means all-knowing, which is being completely informed.

clue.text: Wind indicator that's useless, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for futile is taken by its spoken form

parts.note: vain means futile or useless

explanation.surface: A useless weathercock, people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather vane turns to show which way the wind is blowing.

clue.text: Expert holding right amount of land

indicators.note: holding means the expert's letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist owns the right to a piece of land.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of area used for measuring land.

clue.text: Horse not competing with knight on course

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
a starter is the first course of a meal

explanation.surface: A horse withdrawn from the race, though a knight rides on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a racecourse but means a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-starter is literally a horse that is withdrawn and does not run in a race.
